note.ja: per（完全に）+ cept（つかむ）+ ion。しっかりつかみ取ること →「知覚・認識」。perceive（知覚する）。

en: A practitioner of physic, i.e. a specialist in internal medicine, especially as opposed to a surgeon; a practitioner who treats with medi…
A medical doctor trained in human medicine.

physician.ety: From Middle English fisicien, from Old French fisicïen (“physician”) (modern French physicien (“physicist”)), from fisique (“art of healing”), from Latin physica (“natural science”), from Ancient Greek φυσική ἐπιστήμη (phusikḗ epistḗmē, “knowledge of nature”), from φυσικός (phusikós, “pertaining to nature”). Displaced native Middle English læche, leche, archaic English leech (“physician”). Morphologically physic + -ian.

ex.en: He is the physician I talked about yesterday.
ex.ja: 彼はきのう私が話題にした医者です。

ex.en: A six-figure income isn't uncommon for physicians.
ex.ja: 医者なら６桁の収入は珍しくない。

ex.en: A six-figure income is not uncommon for physicians.
ex.ja: 医者なら６桁の収入は珍しくない。

en: To move, pass, or go forward or onward; to advance; to carry on.
To pass from one point, topic, or stage, to another.

proceed.ety: From Middle English proceden, from Old French proceder, from Latin prōcēdō (“to go forth, go forward, advance”), from prō (“forth”) + cēdō (“to go”); see cede.

ex.en: He proceeded in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険に直面しても進んでいった。

ex.en: He proceeded to the next question.
ex.ja: 次の問題にとりかかった。

ex.en: She then proceeded to negotiate with her bank.
ex.ja: それから彼女は銀行との交渉を続けた。

note.ja: pro（前へ）+ ceed（進む）。前へ進む →「進む・続行する」。

en: A learner at a school under the supervision of a teacher.
One who studies under supervision of a renowned expert in their field.

pupil.ety: From Middle English pupille, from Anglo-Norman pupille (“orphan”), from Latin pūpillus (“orphan, minor”), variant of pūpulus (“little boy”), from pūpus (“child, boy”).

ex.en: How many pupils are there in your school?
ex.ja: あなたの学校には何人の生徒がいますか。

ex.en: He drove a point home to his pupils.
ex.ja: 彼はポイントを生徒に充分わからせた。

ex.en: The pupils are bound down by the rules.
ex.ja: 生徒たちは規制で縛りつけられている。

en: To reestablish, or bring back into existence.
To bring back to good condition from a state of decay or ruin.
The act of recovering data or a system from a backup.

restore.ety: From Middle English restoren, from Old French restorer, from Latin rēstaurāre. By surface analysis, re- + store.

ex.en: After decades of civil war, order was restored.
ex.ja: 数十年の内戦の後に秩序が回復した。

ex.en: How on earth can we restore our youth?
ex.ja: 一体どうしたら若さが取り戻せるのだろう。

ex.en: It was suggested that the tower be restored.
ex.ja: その塔を復元してはどうかと提案された。

en: A firearm fired from the shoulder; improved range and accuracy is provided by a long, rifled barrel.
An artillery piece with a rifled barrel.
To quickly search through many items (such as papers, the contents of a drawer, a pile of clothing).
To commit robbery or theft.

rifle.ety: Originally short for “rifled gun”, referring to the spiral grooves inside the barrel. From Middle English riflen (“to rob, plunder, search through”), from Old French rifler (“to lightly scratch, scrape off, plunder”), from Old High German riffilōn (compare German riffeln (“to score, make grooves in, ripple”), archaic Dutch rijfelen (“to scrape”), Old English rifelan, riflian (“to wrinkle”)), frequentative of Proto-Germanic *rīfaną (compare Old Norse rífa (“to tear, break”)). More at rive.

ex.en: He carried a rifle on his shoulder.
ex.ja: 彼は肩に銃を担いだ。

ex.en: The soldier refused to fire his rifle at the enemy.
ex.ja: その兵士は敵に向けてライフル銃を発射する事を拒否した。

ex.en: Suddenly there was a rifle shot.
ex.ja: 突然ライフルの銃声がした。

en: A competitor (person, team, company, etc.) with the same goal as another, or striving to attain the same thing. Defeating a rival may be …
Someone or something with similar claims of quality or distinction as another.
Having the same pretensions or claims; standing in competition for superiority.
To oppose or compete with.
To be equal to, or match, or to surpass another.

rival.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin rīvālis (literally “person using the same stream as another”). By surface analysis, Latin rīvus + -al.

ex.en: We lost out to our rival in price competition.
ex.ja: 私たちはライバルに価格競争で敗れた。

ex.en: Two rival parties are essential to good democratic government.
ex.ja: 健全な民主主義には対立した二等が不可欠だ。

ex.en: I once rivaled him for the championship.
ex.ja: 私はかつて彼と優勝を争ったことがある。

en: A person who moves, on foot, at a fast pace, especially an athlete.
Any entrant, person or animal (especially a horse), for a race or any competition; a candidate for an election.

runner.ety:
From Middle English rennere, rynner, urnare, equivalent to run + -er. Cognate with Old Norse rennari (“runner; messenger”). Displaced earlier Middle English runel (“runner”), from Old English rynel (“runner”; also “messenger, courier”).
((botany) a long stolon sent by a plant): Compare typologically Russian побе́г (pobég) (akin to бежа́ть (bežátʹ)).

ex.en: Some runners drink water as they are running.
ex.ja: 走者の中には走りながら水を飲む者もいる。

ex.en: Brazil finished runners-up in the 1998 World Cup.
ex.ja: 1998年のワールドカップでは、ブラジルは準優勝に終わった。

ex.en: Some famous foreign runners entered that race.
ex.ja: そのレースには有名外国人のランナーが何人か参加した。

en: In a sad manner; sorrowfully.
Unfortunately, sad to say.

sadly.ety: From Middle English sadly; equivalent to sad + -ly.

ex.en: Sadly, my cat has gone away somewhere.
ex.ja: 悲しいことに私の猫はどこかへいってしまった。

ex.en: Sadly, his dream didn't come true.
ex.ja: 悲しいことに彼の夢は実現しなかった。

ex.en: "He used to love me," she answered sadly.
ex.ja: 以前は愛してくれたのだけれど。と彼女は悲しそうに答えた。

en: The extent to which something matters; importance
Meaning.

significance.ety: Inherited from Middle English significaunce, from Middle French significance, from Old French significance, from Latin significantia. Doublet of signifiance.

ex.en: Your thoughts are of no significance at all.
ex.ja: 君の考えなどはどうだっていいことだ。

ex.en: It has no absolute and universal significance.
ex.ja: それには絶対的で普遍的な意味はない。

ex.en: Recently he has come to realize the significance of married life.
ex.ja: 最近彼は結婚生活の意味がわかるようになった。

en: A metallic salt derived from a fatty acid, commonly used in cleaning products.
Some other substance, often a detergent or another surfactant, able to mix with both oil and water, used for cleaning.
To apply soap to in washing.
To cover, lather, or in any other manner treat with soap, often as a prank.

From Middle English sope, sape, from Old English sāpe (“soap, salve”), from Proto-West Germanic *saipā, from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ, from Proto-Indo-European *seyb-, *seyp- (“to pour out, drip, trickle, strain”).
Cognate with Scots saip, sape (“soap”), Saterland Frisian Seepe (“soap”), West Frisian sjippe (“soap”), Dutch zeep (“soap”), German Low German Seep (“soap”), German Seife (“soap”), Danish sæbe (“soap”), Swedish såpa (“soap”), Norwegian Bokmål såp

ex.en: Wash your hands with a bar of soap.
ex.ja: 石鹸で手を洗いなさい。

ex.en: Why is there soap on the table?
ex.ja: どうして石鹸がテーブルの上にあるの？

ex.en: That boy likes to walk around the soap shop.
ex.ja: その男の子は石鹸の店の周りを歩くのが好き。

en: A fine, gentle, dispersed mist of liquid.
Something resembling a spray of liquid.
To project a liquid in a dispersive manner toward something.
To project in a dispersive manner.

spray.ety:
From Middle Dutch sprāien, sprayen, spraeyen (“to spray, sprinkle, spread”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *sprēwijaną (“to spray, sprinkle”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)per- (“to sow, scatter”).
Cognate with Middle High German spræjen, spræwen (“to squirt, spray, dust, splash, straw”), Danish dialectal språe (“to open up, burst forth”), Swedish dialectal språ (“to sprout, shoot forth, burst”), Norwegian dialectal spra, spræ (“to splash, splatter, spout, burst forth”), Dutch sproeien (“to spray, sprinkle”), German sprühen (“to spray, sparkle”).

ex.en: The waves sprayed the rocks with water.
ex.ja: 波は岩に水しぶきをかけた。

ex.en: They are spraying the fruit trees.
ex.ja: 彼らは果樹に農薬を散布している。

ex.en: She sprayed pesticide on the flowers.
ex.ja: 彼女は花に殺虫剤を振りまいた。

en: Of, relating to, or having structure.
Involving the mechanics of construction.
Structural steel, used in construction.

ex.en: The structural formula for water is H-O-H.
ex.ja: 水の構造式は H-O-H である。

en: A group or train of attendants, servants etc.; a retinue.
A connected series or succession of objects; a number of things used or classed together.

suite.ety: Borrowed from Middle French suite. See also the doublet suit.

ex.en: She had the hotel suite to herself.
ex.ja: 彼女はホテルのスイートルームを独り占めにした。

ex.en: This suite is three times larger than my condominium.
ex.ja: このスイートルームは私の住んでいるマンションの三倍の広さだ。

ex.en: I'd like a suite.
ex.ja: スイートルームをお願いします。

A tropical plant.

ex.ja: 彼らは熱帯魚に興味があるらしかった。

en: Relating to Ukraine or its people or language.
A person from Ukraine or of Ukrainian descent.

ex.ja: ウクライナでの紛争が、世界中の物価を引き上げてしまっている。

ex.ja: 世界で一番美しい女はウクライナの女だ。

ex.ja: ウクライナ語は話せません。

Done in addition to requirements; unrequired.

ex.en: That is unnecessary, damn it!
ex.ja: 余計なことしやがって。

ex.ja: ムダな機能を省いて安くしました。

en: A poetic form with regular meter and a fixed rhyme scheme.
Poetic form in general.
To tell in verse, or poetry.
to educate about, to teach about.

verse.ety: From Middle English vers, from a mixture of Old English fers and Old French vers; both from Latin versus (“a line in writing, and in poetry a verse; (originally) row, furrow”), from vertō (“to turn around”).

ex.en: A collection of her verses has just been published.
ex.ja: 彼女の詩集が出版されたところだ。

ex.en: She is well versed in Spanish literature.
ex.ja: 彼女はスペイン文学に明るいです。

ex.en: He is well versed in foreign affairs.
ex.ja: 彼は外国事情に通じている。

note.ja: ラテン語 versus（向きを変えること）から。vers（向ける）。鋤を返すように行を折り返すもの →「詩・韻文・（歌の）節」。

en: The winner in a fight or contest.

victor.ety: Inherited from Middle English victour, victor, from Anglo-Norman victor, Latin victor (“conqueror”). Doublet of Victor.

en: The yield of grapes or wine from a vineyard or district during one season.
Wine, especially high-quality, identified as to year and vineyard or district of origin.
Of or relating to a vintage, or to wine identified by a specific vintage.
Having an enduring appeal; high-quality.
To harvest (grapes).
To make (wine) from grapes.

vintage.ety: From Middle English vendage, vyndage, from Anglo-Norman vendenge, from Old French vendage, vendenge (cognate with French vendange), from Latin vindēmia (“a gathering of grapes, vintage”), from vīnum (“wine”) + dēmō (“take off or away, remove”), from de (“of; from, away from”) + emō (“take”).

ex.en: What vintage is this wine?
ex.ja: このワインって、何年ものなの？

ex.en: Is this a vintage car?
ex.ja: 旧車ですか。

en: An English unit of land area (symbol: a. or ac.) originally denoting a day's ploughing for a yoke of oxen, now standardized as 4,840 squa…
An area of 10,240 square yards or 4 quarters.

ex.en: I bought an eight-acre farm for my retirement.
ex.ja: 私は退職後のために８エーカーの農場を買った。

ex.en: They sell land by the acre.
ex.ja: 土地はエーカー単位で売っています。

ex.en: The field measures more than 300 acres.
ex.ja: 畑は面積が３００エーカー以上ある。

To fit by alteration; to modify or remodel for a different purpose; to adjust.
Adapted; fit; suited; suitable; apt.

en: The act of adopting.
The state of being adopted; the acceptance of a child of other parents as if they were one's own child.

adoption.ety: Borrowed from French adoption, from Latin adoptio, allied to adoptare (“to adopt”). Equivalent to adopt + -ion.

Without any name acknowledged of a person responsible.

anonymous.ety: Borrowed into English around 1600 from Late Latin anonymus, from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓νώνῠμος (ănṓnŭmos, “without name”), from ᾰ̓ν- (ăn-, “un-”) with ὄνῠμᾰ (ónŭmă), Aeolic and Doric dialectal form of ὄνομᾰ (ónomă, “name”). English equivalent an- + -onymous.

ex.ja: この件では名前を出したくない。

ex.en: We got an anonymous call.
ex.ja: 匿名の電話があったんです。

ex.en: The poem was composed by an anonymous author.
ex.ja: その詩は無名の著者が詠んだ。

Relating to or characteristic of art or artists.

en: The act of attending; the state of being present; presence.
A tally or listing of the persons present.

attendance.ety: From Middle English attendance, from Old French atendance, from atendre (“to attend, listen”).

ex.ja: 出席状況が最終の成績に響きます。

ex.ja: ぜひ会に出席をお願いします。

ex.ja: 母親が、彼の看護にあたってる。

Flying, operating, or operation of aircraft.

aviation.ety: Borrowed from French aviation, derived from Latin avis (“bird”). By surface analysis, avi- + -ation.

ex.en: The aviation expert analyzed the statistics in detail.
ex.ja: その航空専門家は統計を詳細に分析した。

ex.ja: 世界の航空産業は墜落事故についての懸念を募らせている。

To put or to pack in a barrel or barrels.

ex.ja: 共和党は民主党の地方人気とり補助金政策を非難しました。

ex.en: One rotten apple spoils the barrel.
ex.ja: 腐ったリンゴが１つあるとたる全体がだめになる。

en: Much loved, dearly loved.
Someone who is loved; something that is loved.

beloved.ety: From Middle English beloved, biloved, equivalent to belove + -ed.

ex.ja: 彼は大事な犬をとうてい手放すことはできなかった。

en: Tender and amiable; of a considerate or kindly disposition.
Soft and mild rather than hard or severe.
To become gentle.
To break; to tame; to domesticate.
A maggot used as bait by anglers.
A trained falcon, or falcon-gentil.

gentle.ety: From Middle English gentil (“courteous, noble”), from Old French gentil (“high-born, noble”), from Latin gentilis (“of the same family or clan”), from gens (“[Roman] clan”). Doublet of gentile, genteel, and jaunty.

ex.ja: 一見、彼は親切で優しい人のようだった。

ex.ja: 彼の親切な態度にすっかり騙された。

ex.ja: メアリーはベビーシッターにとても優しい。

note.ja: ラテン語 gentilis（同じ一族の・家柄のよい）から。gen（一族）。よい家柄の →「優しい・穏やかな」。gentleman（紳士）。

en: A system of rules and principles for the structure of a language, or of languages in general.
The study of such a system.

grammar.ety: From Middle English gramere, from Old French gramaire (“classical learning”), from unattested Vulgar Latin *grammāria, an alteration of Latin grammatica, from Ancient Greek γραμματική (grammatikḗ, “skilled in writing”), from γράμμα (grámma, “line of writing”), from γράφω (gráphō, “write”), from Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ- (“to carve, scratch”). Displaced native Old English stæfcræft; a doublet of glamour, glamoury, gramarye, and grimoire. Piecewise doublet of grammatic.

note.ja: ギリシャ語 grammatike（文字の技術）から。gram（書かれたもの）。→「文法」。

To provide a book or other publication with pictures, diagrams or other explanatory or decorative features.

en: To design a new process or mechanism.
To create something fictional for a particular purpose.

invent.ety:
From Middle English inventen, borrowed from Old French inventer, from Latin inventus, perfect passive participle of inveniō (“come upon, meet with, find, discover”), from in (“in, on”) + veniō (“come”); see venture. Compare advent, covent, event, prevent, etc.
Displaced native Old English āþenċan (literally “to think out”).

ex.ja: 彼はコンクリートも発明したと言われている。

ex.ja: 作り事はすべて、真実だ。

en: A sweet mixture of fruit boiled with sugar and allowed to congeal. Often spread on bread or toast or used in jam tarts
A difficult situation.
To get something stuck, often (though not necessarily) in a confined space.
To brusquely force something into a space; to cram, to squeeze.

jam.ety:
First attested in the early 18th c. as a verb meaning “to press, be pressed, be wedged in”. Compare dialectal jammock (“to press, squeeze, crush into a soft mass, chew food"; also "a soft, pulpy substance”). Perhaps from Middle English chammen, champen ("to bite upon something, gnash the teeth"; whence modern champ, chomp), of uncertain origin; probably originally onomatopoeic.
The "performance" sense is first attested with regards to jazz in 1929, and its origin, though uncertain, is likely metaphorical, "something sweet made by the combination of many things", with influence from jamboree.

ex.en: We met a traffic jam on the way.

To hold a lease as a tenant; to rent.

lease.ety: From Middle English *lesen, from Anglo-Norman *leser, Old French lesser, laisier (“to let, let go”), partly from Latin laxō (“to loose”) and partly from Old High German lāzan (“to let, let go, release”) (German lassen), cognate with Old English lǣtan (“to allow, let go, leave, rent”) whence let.

Having unknown qualities.

A sentiment; an opinion.

ex.ja: 私はこのような考えをずっと前にすっかり捨ててしまった。

ex.ja: 彼の考えはいわゆる進歩的なものだった。

To take the partial regression coefficient.

partial.ety: From Middle English partiall, parcial, from Old French parcial (“biased or particular”), from Late Latin partiālis (“of or pertaining to a part”), from Latin pars (“part”).

ex.en: She is in partial agreement with this decision.
ex.ja: 彼女はこの決定に部分的に同意している。

ex.en: He is always partial to the company of girls.
ex.ja: 彼はいつも女の子を贔屓する。

ex.en: The play was only a partial success.
ex.ja: その芝居は部分的な成功しかおさめなかった。

To hunt or kill rats.
To betray a political party, cause or principle; to betray someone, to desert a person or thing.

rat.ety:
From Middle English raat, rat, ratt, ratte, rotte, from Old English ræt, rætt, from Proto-West Germanic *ratt, from Proto-Germanic *rattaz, *rattō (“rat”), of uncertain origin, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *Hreh₃d- (“to gnaw, scrape, scratch”). Cognates

ex.ja: ねずみが壁に穴をあけた。

en: The act of reflecting or the state of being reflected.
The property of a propagated wave being thrown back from a surface (such as a mirror).

reflection.ety: From Middle English refleccion, refleccioun, refleccioune, reflection, from Middle French reflection, reflexion, and its source Late Latin reflexiō, from the participle stem of reflectō. The current spelling is influenced by reflect. Equivalent to reflect + -ion.

ex.en: I'm looking at my reflection in the lake.
ex.ja: 僕は湖に映った自分の姿を見てるんです。

ex.en: She is a reflection of her mother.
ex.ja: 彼女は母親にそっくりだ。

ex.en: His bad behavior is a reflection on his common sense.
ex.ja: 行儀の悪さは彼の良識を疑わせるものだ。

en: To find a solution to (a problem).
To reduce to simple or intelligible notions; to make clear or certain; to unravel; to explain.
Determination; will power.
A determination to do something; a fixed decision.

resolve.ety: From Middle English resolven, from Old French resolver, a learned borrowing of Latin resolvō (“loosen, thaw, melt, resolve”), equivalent to re- + solve. Piecewise doublet of re-solve.

ex.en: We had a hard time resolving that problem.
ex.ja: その問題を解決するのに苦労したんだよ。

ex.en: This liquid can be resolved into three elements.
ex.ja: この液体は３つの要素に分解できる。

ex.en: He made a resolve to stop smoking.
ex.ja: タバコをやめようと彼は決心した。

en: Of or pertaining to a revolution in government; tending to, or promoting, revolution
Of or pertaining to something that portends of great change; overthrowing a standing mindset
A revolutionist; a person who revolts.

revolutionary.ety: Compare French révolutionnaire; equivalent to revolution + -ary.

ex.en: The revolutionary council met to plan strategy.
ex.ja: 革命評議委員会は戦略の計画を立てるために集まった。

ex.en: The most radical revolutionary will become a conservative the day after the revolution.
ex.ja: 最も急進的な革命家が革命の翌日には保守になる。

ex.en: This invention is so revolutionary, it might make it into the textbooks.
ex.ja: これは、画期的な発明だから教科書に載るかもよ。

note.ja: revolution（革命）+ ary。大転換の →「革命の・画期的な」。

en: An incident or event that disgraces or damages the reputation of the persons or organization involved.
Damage to one's reputation.

scandal.ety:
From Middle French scandale (“indignation caused by misconduct or defamatory speech”), from Ecclesiastical Latin scandalum (“that on which one trips, cause of offense”, literally “stumbling block”), from Ancient Greek σκάνδαλον (skándalon, “a trap laid for an enemy, a cause of moral stumbling”), from Proto-Indo-European *skand- (“to jump”). Cognate with Latin scandō (“to climb”). First attested from Old Northern French escandle, but the modern word is a reborrowing. Doublet, via Old French esclandre, of slander.
Sense evolution from "cause of stumbling, that which causes one to sin, stumbling

ex.ja: スキャンダルは彼の清潔なイメージを酷く傷つけた。

ex.ja: 彼らはその汚職と何か関係がある。

en: To emit or reflect light so as to glow.
To reflect light.

Brightness from reflected light.

shine.ety:

ex.ja: 試合は雨天決行です。

A substitute teacher.

ex.ja: 機械を人の代わりにするのは不可能だ。

en: That which causes wonder; a prodigy; a portent.
To become filled with wonderment or admiration; to be amazed at something.

marvel.ety: First attested from 1300, from Middle English merveile, from Old French merveille (“a wonder”), from Vulgar Latin *miribilia, from Latin mīrābilia (“wonderful things”), from neuter plural of mīrābilis (“strange, wonderful”), from mīror (“to wonder at”), from mīrus (“wonderful”). ex.en: The marvel is that he knew it.
ex.ja: 不思議なのは彼がそれを知っていたことだ。

ex.en: It is a marvel that he should say so.
ex.ja: 彼がそう言うなんて不思議だ。

ex.en: I marvel how you could agree to the proposal.
ex.ja: 君がなぜ提案に賛成なのか不思議だ。

en: In addition to what has been said.

moreover.ety: Inherited from Middle English moreover, moreovere, morover, mooreover, more-overe, mare over, equivalent to more + over.

ex.ja: それにいくら払ったの？

ex.en: His house is small and moreover it's old.
ex.ja: 彼の住居は小さくてそれに古い。

ex.en: The bag was big, and moreover, it was heavy.
ex.ja: その袋は大きかった。おまけに重かった。

en: Synonym of military parade: A show of troops, an assembly of troops as a show of force, to receive orders, or especially for inspection a…
A public procession, especially one commemorating a holiday or special event or (dated) in protest.
To assemble for inspection, to receive orders, etc.
To march impressively or ostentatiously.

parade.ety: From French parade (“an ostentatious display, a military display”), from parer (“to beautify, prepare, take pride in”) + -ade probably under influence from earlier Italian parata (“preparation, a military parade, an ostentatious display”) and Latin magnō parātū (“with great preparation”). Various senses similarly influenced by earlier French and Italian uses. Doublet of pare.

ex.en: The parade was led by an army band.
ex.ja: そのパレードは軍楽隊に先導された。

ex.en: Boys and girls were parading along the street.
ex.ja: 少年少女たちが通りでパレードしていた。

ex.en: Don't make such a parade of your wealth.
ex.ja: 財産をそんなに見せびらかす物ではない。

en: The place where sanctified souls are believed to live after death.
A very pleasant place, such as a place full of lush vegetation.
To place (as) in paradise.

paradise.ety: From Middle English paradis, paradise, paradys, from Late Old English paradīs, borrowed from Old French paradis, from Latin paradīsus, from Ancient Greek παράδεισος (parádeisos), ultimately from Proto-Iranian *paridayjah. Doublet of parvis. Displaced Old English neorxnawang.

ex.en: This park is a paradise for children.
ex.ja: この公園は子供の楽園だ。

ex.en: The island is a paradise for children.
ex.ja: その島は子供にとっては楽園です。

ex.en: This beach is a paradise for surfers.
ex.ja: このビーチはサーファーにはパラダイスだ。

en: To become aware of, through the physical senses, to see; to understand.
To interpret something in a particular way.

perceive.ety: From Middle English perceyven, borrowed from Old French percevoir, perceveir, from Latin percipiō, past participle perceptus (“take hold of, obtain, receive, observe”), from per (“by, through”) + capiō (“to take”); see capable. Compare conceive, deceive, receive.

ex.en: Nobody perceived me entering the room.
ex.ja: 誰も私が部屋に入って来たことに気づかなかった。

ex.en: I perceive by your face that you have good news.
ex.ja: あなたの表情から良い知らせがあるとすぐ分かります。

ex.en: They're cleverly changing how we perceive them.
ex.ja: 巧妙にイメージがすり替えられている。

note.ja: per（完全に）+ ceiv（つかむ）+ e。しっかりつかみ取る →「知覚する・気づく」。

en: In preparation for the main matter; initial, introductory, preparatory.
A preparation for a main matter; an introduction.
Any of a series of sports events that determine the finalists.

preliminary.ety: Borrowed from New Latin praelīmināris, formed from prae- (“before”) + līmen (“threshold”) + -āris (adjectival suffix); compare Latin līmināris (“of or belonging to a threshold”). Compare French préliminaire.

ex.en: Regretfully, the Japanese representative was eliminated at the preliminary stage.
ex.ja: 日本代表は惜しくも予選敗退となりました。

en: The first showing of a film, play or other form of entertainment, often held as a special event with celebrity guests.
The first episode of a television show or a particular season of that show.
Of a film or play, to play for the first time.
To present a film or play for the first time.

ex.en: I guarantee a huge audience for tonight's premiere.
ex.ja: 今夜の初日はきっと大にぎわいになりますよ。

en: The office or role of president.
The bureaucratic organization and governmental initiatives devolving directly from the president.

presidency.ety: From Medieval Latin praesidentia. By surface analysis, president + -cy.

ex.ja: 彼は大統領に立候補するだろう。

ex.en: He made a hard run of the presidency.
ex.ja: 彼は大統領選挙で懸命に戦った。

ex.ja: 私があなただったら、その古い帽子を取っておくだろうに。

ex.ja: コンピューターを使えば情報を保持することができる。

ex.en: This town still retains something of the old days.
ex.ja: この町はいまだに昔の面影をとどめている。

en: A fulfilment of a need or desire.
The pleasure obtained by the fulfillment of one or more needs or desires; a sense of contentment with one's situation and achievements.

satisfaction.ety: From Middle English satisfaccioun, from Old French satisfaccion and Latin satisfactiō, satisfactiōnis.

ex.ja: これはきっと気に入って頂けると思います。

ex.en: His success was a great satisfaction to me.
ex.ja: 彼の成功は私にとって大きな喜びでした。

ex.ja: そうしてもらったら私は満足だ。

en: To rub a surface with a sharp object, especially by a living creature to remove itching with nails, claws, etc.

A disruption, mark or shallow cut on a surface made by scratching.
An act of scratching the skin to alleviate an itch or irritation.
For or consisting of preliminary or tentative, incomplete, etc. work.
Hastily assembled, arranged or constructed, from whatever materials are to hand, with little or no preparation

scratch.ety:

sheriff.ety: Inherited from Middle English shirreve, in turn inherited from Old English sċīrġerēfa, corresponding to shire + reeve. ex.ja: 保安官は、その町の秩序を確立した。

Reserved; disinclined to familiar approach.

ex.ja: 彼女は高校時代内気でした。

ex.en: He is too shy to talk to girls.

ex.en: The fact is that my cat is shy.
ex.ja: 実はわたしの猫は恥ずかしがり屋なのです。

Former, erstwhile; at some previous time.
Occasional; intermittent.

ex.ja: またお会いできるといいですね。

ex.en: No, I don't. I want to learn sometime.

ex.ja: 速い者が競争に勝つとは限らない。

ex.en: Life is short and time is swift.
ex.ja: 人生は短く、時がたつのは速い。

ex.en: The stream is not very swift.
ex.ja: 流れはさほど速くない。

en: A device for grasping an object and an attached means of moving it, as a rope and hook.
A block and tackle.
To force a person to the ground with the weight of one's own body, usually by jumping on top or slamming one's weight into them.
To face or deal with, attempting to overcome or fight down.

tackle.ety: From Middle English takel (“gear, apparatus”), from Middle Dutch or Middle Low German takel (“ship's rigging”), perhaps related to Middle Dutch taken (“to grasp, seize”). Akin to Danish takkel (“tackle”), Swedish tackel (“tackle”). More at take.

ex.en: To begin with, we must tackle the problem.
ex.ja: まず第１に、私たちはその問題に取り組まなければならない。

ex.en: Let's tackle this problem from a different angle.
ex.ja: この問題を別の面から取り組んでみよう。

ex.en: The writer is tackling the now new novel.
ex.ja: その作家は今新しい小説に取り組んでいる。

en: A graphical representation of a chronological sequence of events (past or future).
The feed of a social media service, especially when ordered chronologically.
To analyse a sequence of events or activities.
To display such a sequence graphically.
The infliction of severe pain or anguish, especially as an interrogation technique or punishment; (usually in the plural) a technique, me…
Sexual activity involving the infliction of pain to a certain body part or in a certain manner.
To intentionally inflict severe pain or suffering on (someone), usually with the aim of forcing confessions or punishing them.

torture.ety: From Middle English torture, from Old French torture, from Late Latin tortūra (“a twisting, writhing, of bodily pain, a griping colic;” in Medieval Latin “pain inflicted by judicial or ecclesiastical authority as a means of persuasion, torture”), from Latin tortus (whence also tort), past participle of torquēre (“to twist”).

ex.en: Tom was tortured by the police.
ex.ja: トムは警察で拷問を受けた。

ex.en: He was subjected to torture by the police.
ex.ja: 彼は警察で拷問を受けた。

ex.en: His lecture on chemistry was nothing but torture.
ex.ja: 彼の化学の講義は苦痛以外のなにものでもなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 torquere（ねじる）から。tort + ure。体をねじること →「拷問・苦痛」。

en: To change spoken words or written text (of a book, document, movie, etc.) from one language to another.
To provide a translation of spoken words or written text in another language; to be, or be capable of being, rendered in another language.
In Euclidean spaces: a set of points obtained by adding a given fixed vector to each point of a given set.

translate.ety:
From Middle English translaten (“to transport, translate, transform”), from Anglo-Norman translater, from Latin trānslātus, perfect passive participle of trānsferō (“to transport, carry across, translate”). See also -ate (verb-forming suffix). Distant doublet of transfer, see collate and confer, delate and defer, as well as prelate and prefer among others.
In this sense, displaced Old English wendan (“to translate,” also the word for “to turn” and “to change”).

ex.en: There are some things that can't be translated.
ex.ja: 翻訳できないものもありますよ。

ex.en: How would you translate this sentence into French?
ex.ja: この文をフランス語にどう翻訳しますか？

ex.en: Can you help me translate this into French?
ex.ja: これをフランス語に翻訳するのを手伝ってくれない？

note.ja: trans（向こうへ）+ lat（運ばれた）+ e。向こう側へ運ぶ →「翻訳する・置き換える」。

en: Requiring immediate attention.
Of people: insistent, solicitous.

urgent.ety: Borrowed from Middle French urgent (“pressing, impelling”), from Latin urgēns, from urgēre (“to press”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵʰ- (“bind, squeeze”). Equivalent to urge + -ent. Related to German würgen (“to strangle”), Lithuanian ver̃žti (“to string, tighten, constrict”), Russian (poetic) отверза́ть (otverzátʹ, “to open”, literally “to untie”), Polish otwierać (“to open”)) and English worry, wring, wreak, wreck.

ex.en: He had some urgent news to tell me.
ex.ja: 彼には僕に話したい緊急の知らせがあった。

ex.en: I have an urgent matter to attend to.
ex.ja: 急いでする事がある。

ex.en: There is an urgent need for social change.
ex.ja: 社会の変革が急務である。

en: A plant raised for some edible part of it, such as the leaves, roots, fruit or flowers, but excluding any plant considered to be a fruit,…
The edible part of such a plant.
Of or relating to plants.
Of or relating to vegetables.

ex.en: Fresh vegetables are very expensive in the winter.
ex.ja: 冬は新鮮な野菜は高値である。

ex.en: Be a good boy and eat your vegetables.
ex.ja: いい子だから野菜を食べなさい。

ex.en: What do you call this vegetable in English?
ex.ja: この野菜は英語で何と言いますか。

en: Standing, pointing, or moving straight up or down; parallel to the local direction of gravity; along the direction of a plumb line; perpe…
In a two-dimensional Cartesian co-ordinate system, describing the axis y oriented normal (perpendicular, at right angles) to the horizont…
A vertex or zenith.
A vertical geometrical figure; a perpendicular.

vertical.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vertical, from Late Latin verticālis.

ex.en: He drew some vertical lines on the paper.
ex.ja: 彼は紙のうえに垂直な線を何本か引いた。

ex.en: Strictly speaking, it was not a vertical line.
ex.ja: 厳密に言えば、それは垂直線ではなかった。

ex.en: Keep away from the vertical cliff!
ex.ja: その切り立った崖には近づかないで。

note.ja: ラテン語 vertex（頂点・回転軸）から。vert（回る）。頂点に向かう →「垂直の・縦の」。

en: An infraction or a failure to follow a rule.
Rape; sexual activity forced on another person without their consent.

violation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French violation, from Latin violātiō (“injury, profanation”), from violō (“to treat with violence; to maltreat; to violate, defile, profane”). Morphologically violate + -ion.

ex.en: I don't agree with violation of human rights.
ex.ja: 私は人権侵害に反対だ。

ex.en: The local police are very strict about traffic violations.
ex.ja: 地元の警察は交通違反にはとても厳しい。

ex.en: I was fined six thousand yen for a parking violation.
ex.ja: 駐車違反で６０００円の罰金をとられた。

en: A small case, often flat and often made of leather, for keeping money (especially paper money), credit cards, etc.
A person's bank account or assets.

wallet.ety: From Middle English walet (“a bag, knapsack”), of uncertain origin. Possibly from an assumed Old Northern French *walet (“a roll; bag; a knapsack”), from Proto-Germanic *wal- (“to roll”). More at walk, well, wallow.

ex.en: I finally managed to find my lost wallet.
ex.ja: 私はなくした財布をとうとう見つけることができた。

ex.en: He felt in his pocket for his wallet.
ex.ja: 彼はポケットの中に手を入れて財布を探しました。

ex.en: When did you notice your wallet was missing?
ex.ja: いつ財布がないのに気付いたの？

en: A room, especially one which is not particularly large, used for manufacturing or other light industrial work.
A brief, intensive course of education for a small group, emphasizing interaction and practical problem solving.
To help a playwright revise a draft of (a play) by rehearsing it with actors and critiquing the results.
To work on or revise something, especially collaboratively, in a workshop.

ex.en: He's making a table in his workshop.
ex.ja: 彼は仕事場でテーブルを作っているところだ。

ex.en: The basement has been made over into a workshop.
ex.ja: 地下室を仕事場に改造した。

ex.en: Please give us a call now if you want to participate in the workshop.
ex.ja: この講習会に参加をご希望のかたは、今すぐお電話ください。

en: On board; into or within a ship or boat; hence, into or within a railway car.
On or onto a horse, a camel, etc.
On board of; onto or into a ship, boat, train, plane.
Onto a horse.

aboard.ety: From Middle English abord, from a- (“on”) + bord (“board, side of a ship”); equivalent to a- + board.

ex.en: How many people were aboard that ship?
ex.ja: その船には何人の人が乗ってたんですか？

ex.en: It was my first trip aboard.
ex.ja: 初めての海外旅行でした。

ex.en: They are now aboard the ship.
ex.ja: 彼らは今船に乗っている。

en: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.
Something that concentrates in itself the qualities of a larger item, or multiple items.
Not concrete: conceptual, ideal.
Insufficiently factual.
To separate; to disengage.
To remove; to take away; withdraw.

abstract.ety: From Middle English abstract, borrowed from Latin abstractus, perfect passive participle of abstrahō (“draw away”), formed from abs- (“away”) + trahō (“to pull, draw”). The verbal sense is first attested in 1542.

ex.en: His speech is too abstract to understand.
ex.ja: 彼の演説は抽象的なので私には理解できない。

ex.en: Your explanation is too abstract to me.
ex.ja: あなたの説明は私には抽象的すぎます。

ex.en: Abstract art is not to the taste of everyone.
ex.ja: 抽象芸術が万人の好みに合うとは限らない。

note.ja: abs（離れて）+ tract（引く）。具体物から引き離した →「抽象的な・要約」。

en: A higher-pitched or stronger (louder or longer) articulation of a particular syllable of a word or phrase in order to distinguish it from…
Emphasis or importance in general.
To express the accent of vocally; to utter with accent.
To mark emphatically; to emphasize; to accentuate; to make prominent.

ex.ja: トムは強いフランス語訛りの英語を話す。

ex.en: His policy puts the accent on national welfare.
ex.ja: 彼の政策は国民の福祉に重点を置く。

en: A state that is characterized by compulsive drug use or compulsive engagement in rewarding behavior, despite negative consequences.
The state of being addicted; devotion; inclination.

addiction.ety: From addict + -ion; compare (Latin) addictio (“an adjudging, an award”).

ex.en: Drug addiction is a cancer in modern society.
ex.ja: 麻薬中毒は現代社会の癌だ。

ex.en: There really is such a thing as Internet addiction.
ex.ja: インターネット中毒って、本当にあるみたいね。

ex.en: Tom has been in clinical treatment for addiction for the last five years.
ex.ja: トムはここ5年、嗜癖の臨床治療を続けています。

en: Not asleep; conscious.
Alert, aware.
To become conscious after having slept.
To cause (somebody) to stop sleeping.

ex.en: Take care not to awake the sleeping baby.
ex.ja: 眠っている赤ん坊を起こさないように注意しなさい。

ex.en: When I awoke, he had already been there.
ex.ja: 私が目を覚ましたとき、彼はすでにそこにいた。

ex.en: When I awoke this morning, I felt hungry.
ex.ja: 今朝目が覚めたとき、空腹感を覚えた。

en: Any large piece of timber or iron long in proportion to its thickness, and prepared for use.
One of the principal horizontal structural members, usually of steel, timber, or concrete, of a building.
To emit beams of light; to shine; to radiate.
To smile broadly or especially cheerfully.

ex.en: This program is beamed from US to Japan.
ex.ja: この番組はアメリカから日本へ送られている。

ex.en: We beamed the message to the world.
ex.ja: 我々は世界中にそのメッセージを送った。

ex.en: Beams bear the weight of the roof.
ex.ja: 梁が屋根をささえている。

en: Any plant of several genera of the taxonomic family Fabaceae that produces large edible seeds or edible seedpods.
The large edible seed of such a plant (for example, a broad bean, navy bean, or garbanzo bean).
To hit with a projectile, especially a deliberately aimed blow to the head.

ex.en: I want to eat rice with beans.
ex.ja: 豆ご飯が食べたいな。

ex.en: Brazil supplies the world with coffee beans of quality.
ex.ja: ブラジルは世界に良質のコーヒー豆を供給しています。

ex.en: The man returned from his vacation full of beans.
ex.ja: その男は元気いっぱい、休暇から戻ってきた。

en: Free from writing, printing, or marks; having an empty space to be filled in.
Lacking characteristics which give variety; uniform.
The white spot in the centre of a target; hence (figuratively) the object to which anything is directed or aimed, the range of such aim.
A lot by which nothing is gained; a ticket in a lottery on which no prize is indicated.
To make void; to erase.
To render ineffective by blanketing with turbulent airflow, such as from aircraft wake or reverse thrust.

blank.ety: From Middle English blank, blonc, blaunc, blaunche, from Anglo-Norman blonc, blaunc, blaunche, from Old French blanc, feminine blanche, from Frankish *blank (“gleaming, white, blinding”), from Proto-Germanic *blankaz (“white, bright, blinding”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰleyǵ- (“to shine”). Akin to Old High German blanch (“shining, bright, white”) (German blank), Old English blanc (“white, grey”), blanca (“white steed”), Spanish blanco. More at blink, blind, blanch. Doublet of blanc.

ex.en: Begin to write, leaving one space blank.
ex.ja: １ます空けて書き出しなさい。

ex.en: He told me point-blank that I was fired.
ex.ja: お前は首だ、と彼は藪から棒に私に告げた。

ex.en: My memory is blank on the subject.
ex.ja: その問題では記憶がぜんぜんない。

en: An animal from the subtribe Bubalina, also known as true buffalos, such as the Cape buffalo, Syncerus caffer, or the water buffalo, Bubal…
A related North American animal, the American bison, Bison bison.
To hunt buffalo.

buffalo.ety: Borrowed from Portuguese or Spanish búfalo (“buffalo”), from Late Latin būfalus, from Latin būbalus, from Ancient Greek βούβαλος (boúbalos, “antelope, wild ox”). Doublet of bubale and buffle.

ex.en: Hundreds of buffaloes moved toward the lake.
ex.ja: 何百というバッファローが湖のほうへ移動した。

ex.en: Is that a cow or a buffalo?
ex.ja: あれは牛ですか水牛ですか。

ex.en: A buffalo is akin to an ox.
ex.ja: 水牛は牛に似ている。

en: A firmly held belief.
A judgement of guilt in a court of law.

conviction.ety: From late Middle English conviction, from Anglo-Norman conviction, from Latin convictiō, from convictus, the past participle of convincō (“to convict”). Equivalent to convict + -ion.

ex.en: She always stands up for her convictions.
ex.ja: 彼女は常に自分の信念を弁護している。

ex.en: It is hard to live up to your convictions.
ex.ja: 信念にしたがって行動するのは難しい。

ex.en: His words carry little conviction.
ex.ja: 彼の言葉は説得力がほとんどない。

note.ja: con（完全に）+ vict（打ち勝つ）+ ion。完全に打ち負かされて納得すること →「確信」、法廷で打ち負かすこと →「有罪判決」。

en: Willing to act dishonestly for personal gain; accepting bribes.
In a depraved state; debased; perverted; morally degenerate; weak in morals.
To make corrupt; to change from good to bad; to draw away from the right path; to deprave; to pervert.
To introduce errors; to place into an invalid state.

corrupt.ety: From Middle English corrupten, derived from Latin corruptus, past participle of corrumpō (“to destroy, ruin, injure, spoil, corrupt, bribe”), from com- (“together”) + rumpō (“to break in pieces”).

ex.en: Dan discovered that Matt was a corrupt cop.
ex.ja: ダンはマットが汚職警官であることに気付いた。

ex.en: That organization is corrupt to the core.
ex.ja: あの組織は芯まで、腐っている。

ex.en: That organization is corrupt to its core.
ex.ja: あの組織は芯まで、腐っている。

note.ja: cor（完全に）+ rupt（壊す）。すっかり壊れた →「腐敗した・堕落させる」。

Any member of the species Bos taurus that is not of a bucking breed or fighting breed, regardless of sex or age, including steers and cal…
To intimidate; to daunt the spirits or courage of.

Cognate with Sanskrit गो (go), Ancient Greek βοῦς (boûs), Persian گاو (gâv)), Latvian govs (“cow”), Proto-Slavic *govędo (Serbo-Croatian govedo, Russian говядина (govjadina, “beef”), Scots coo (“cow”), North Frisian ko, kø (“cow”), West Frisian ko (“cow”), Dutch koe (“cow”), Low German Koh, Ko

ex.en: You can wait till the cows come home.
ex.ja: いつまででも待つがいいさ。

ex.en: I have one thousand and five hundred cows.
ex.ja: 私は1500頭の牛を飼育している。

ex.en: Be careful! There's a cow in the road!
ex.ja: 気をつけて！道路に牛がいるんだ。

en: A bend, such as in a road.
A simple figure containing no straight portions and no angles; a curved line.
To bend; to crook.
To cause to swerve from a straight course.

curve.ety: Attested since the 1690s, from Latin curvus (“bent, curved”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker- (“to bend, curve, turn”) + *-wós. Doublet of curb, shrink, carcer, and cancer.

ex.en: The boy knows how to throw a curve.
ex.ja: その少年はカーブの投げ方を知っている。

ex.en: It's a long road with no curves.
ex.ja: 曲り角のないのは長い道である。

ex.en: The road curves to the left around the building.
ex.ja: 道路はその建物のところで左にカーブしている。

en: To press down.
To make depressed, sad or bored.

depress.ety: From Middle English depressen, from Old French depresser, from Latin dēpressus, perfect participle of dēprimō (“to press down, to weigh down”), from dē- (“off, away, down, out”) + premō (“to press”).

ex.en: Tom is depressed because his girlfriend left him.
ex.ja: トムは彼女にふられて落ち込んでいる。

ex.en: I can't believe that he is that depressed.
ex.ja: 彼がそれほど落ち込んでいるとは思えないな。

ex.en: Tom seems a bit depressed this morning.
ex.ja: トム、今朝は少し落ち込んでるみたい。

note.ja: de（下へ）+ press（押す）。押し下げる →「落ち込ませる・不景気にする」。

en: Eating dinner as a social function.
Entertaining someone to dinner.

ex.en: What do you say to dining out together?
ex.ja: 一緒に食事に出かけませんか。

ex.en: What do you say to dining out tonight?
ex.ja: 今夜外で食事をしませんか。

ex.en: She kept the dining room warm in winter.
ex.ja: 彼女は冬に食堂を暖かくしておいた。

The time taken for the current situation to end, especially the current war.

ex.ja: オリンピック選手は、大会期間中は選手村で生活します。
